Explore the /testbed repository (GitHub CLI) to gather information needed for implementing a `safeurl` package and refactoring HTTP request paths. Report back in under 500 words:

1. Check if there's an existing `.github/codeql` directory or similar CodeQL custom query directory. List its contents and describe the structure of any existing custom queries (query file, qhelp file, test directory structure, qlpack.yml).

2. Look at `/testbed/internal/ghrepo/repo.go` or similar - find how repos are typically represented (owner/name).

3. Find 10-15 representative call sites of `apiClient.REST(`, `client.REST(`, `http.NewRequest(`, `http.NewRequestWithContext(`, `httpClient.Get(`, `httpClient.Post(` that use `fmt.Sprintf` or string concatenation with variables in paths. List file paths and brief snippets showing the pattern (especially branch deletion, workflow contents, git refs like tags, secrets, variables, environments).

4. Check go.mod for Go version and module name.

5. Look at `/testbed/pkg/cmd/api/` directory - the `api` command is likely the main one that passes arbitrary paths. How does it handle the path argument?

6. Check `/testbed/internal/ghinstance/host.go` to see how REST prefixes are formed.

7. List existing CodeQL-related files: `.github/workflows/codeql*`, `.github/codeql/`.

Report file paths and concise snippets. Don't paste large files.

Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. 3	# This config extends the default `security-and-quality` suite with the
4	# custom queries in `.github/codeql/queries/`. The custom queries enforce
5	# project-specific invariants that are not covered by the stock packs:
6	#
7	#   - unsanitized-response-to-terminal.ql: HTTP response content that
8	#     reaches a terminal writer (`os.Stdout` / `os.Stderr` /
9	#     `iostreams.IOStreams.Out` / `ErrOut`) other than `ContentOut`
10	#     without being sanitized. Writing to `ContentOut`, calling
11	#     `iostreams.Untrusted.String`, wrapping with `asciisanitizer`, or
12	#     decoding as structured JSON are accepted, so untrusted response
13	#     content is sanitized before it can reach a terminal.
14	#
15	# This config is only meaningful for the Go matrix entry; the Actions
16	# matrix entry ignores it.
17	queries:
18	  - uses: security-and-quality
19	  - uses: ./.github/codeql/queries

1	/**
2	 * @name HTTP response content reaches a terminal without ContentOut or sanitization
3	 * @description Raw bytes consumed from an HTTP response body, or reintroduced by
4	 *              decoding base64, must either be written to `IOStreams.ContentOut`
5	 *              or wrapped with the asciisanitizer before reaching a terminal
6	 *              writer. The body is tracked across function boundaries, so a body
7	 *              returned from a fetch helper and consumed by its caller is still
8	 *              covered. Values produced by structured decoding (encoding/json)
9	 *              are trusted, since cli/cli's REST clients sanitize JSON bodies at
10	 *              the transport layer before decoding.
11	 * @kind path-problem
12	 * @problem.severity error
13	 * @precision medium
14	 * @id cli-cli/unsanitized-response-to-terminal
15	 * @tags security
16	 */
17	
18	import go
19	import semmle.go.dataflow.TaintTracking
20	
21	// ContentOut is the blessed sanitizing writer. Writing raw content there is the
22	// safe choice, so it is excluded from the terminal sink set below.
23	predicate isContentOutRead(DataFlow::Node n) {
24	  exists(Field f |
25	    f.hasQualifiedName("github.com/cli/cli/v2/pkg/iostreams", "IOStreams", "ContentOut") and
26	    n = f.getARead()
27	  )
28	}
29	
30	// Value flow from a ContentOut read so a ContentOut writer stored in a local
31	// variable is still recognised as the blessed sink. Plain DataFlow (not taint)
32	// is used so it does not leak across sibling fields of a shared IOStreams.
33	module ContentOutWriterConfig implements DataFlow::ConfigSig {
34	  predicate isSource(DataFlow::Node n) { isContentOutRead(n) }
35	
36	  predicate isSink(DataFlow::Node n) { exists(n) }
37	}
38	
39	module ContentOutWriterFlow = DataFlow::Global<ContentOutWriterConfig>;
40	
41	predicate isContentOutWriter(DataFlow::Node n) {
42	  isContentOutRead(n) or
43	  exists(DataFlow::Node src | isContentOutRead(src) and ContentOutWriterFlow::flow(src, n))
44	}
45	
46	// ANSI injection requires bytes to reach a terminal. The terminal-bound writers
47	// are os.Stdout / os.Stderr and the IOStreams.Out / IOStreams.ErrOut fields.
48	// File, socket, and buffer writers are not terminals and are intentionally out
49	// of scope.
50	predicate isTerminalWriterRead(DataFlow::Node n) {
51	  (
52	    exists(Variable v |
53	      v.hasQualifiedName("os", "Stdout") or v.hasQualifiedName("os", "Stderr")
54	    |
55	      n = v.getARead()
56	    )
57	    or
58	    exists(Field f |
59	      f.hasQualifiedName("github.com/cli/cli/v2/pkg/iostreams", "IOStreams", "Out") or
60	      f.hasQualifiedName("github.com/cli/cli/v2/pkg/iostreams", "IOStreams", "ErrOut")
61	    |
62	      n = f.getARead()
63	    )
64	  ) and
65	  not isContentOutRead(n)
66	}
67	
68	// Value flow from a terminal-writer read so aliased writers
69	// (`w := opts.IO.Out; fmt.Fprint(w, ...)`) still count as terminal sinks. Plain
70	// DataFlow (not taint) is used so it does not leak across sibling fields of a
71	// shared IOStreams (which would otherwise mark ContentOut as terminal-bound).
72	module TerminalWriterConfig implements DataFlow::ConfigSig {
73	  predicate isSource(DataFlow::Node n) { isTerminalWriterRead(n) }
74	
75	  predicate isSink(DataFlow::Node n) { exists(n) }
76	}
77	
78	module TerminalWriterFlow = DataFlow::Global<TerminalWriterConfig>;
79	
80	predicate isTerminalBoundWriter(DataFlow::Node n) {
81	  isTerminalWriterRead(n) or
82	  exists(DataFlow::Node src | isTerminalWriterRead(src) and TerminalWriterFlow::flow(src, n))
83	}
84	
85	// Raw HTTP body reader. Sourcing at the field read (rather than a local
86	// consumption call) lets global taint carry the reader across returns and
87	// parameters before anything reads it.
88	predicate isResponseBodyReader(DataFlow::Node n) {
89	  exists(Field bodyField |
90	    bodyField.hasQualifiedName("net/http", "Response", "Body") and
91	    n = bodyField.getARead()
92	  )
93	}
94	
95	// Base64 decoding reintroduces raw bytes that any text sanitization applied to
96	// the encoded form never saw, so the decoded stream is its own source.
97	predicate isBase64DecodeSource(DataFlow::Node n) {
98	  exists(DataFlow::CallNode c |
99	    c.getTarget().hasQualifiedName("encoding/base64", "NewDecoder") and n = c
100	  )
101	  or
102	  exists(DataFlow::MethodCallNode c |
103	    c.getTarget().hasQualifiedName("encoding/base64", "Encoding", "DecodeString") and n = c
104	  )
105	}
106	
107	// Carry taint from a reader value into the bytes a read produces, so the flow
108	// continues from the reader to wherever those bytes are written.
109	predicate isReaderConsumptionStep(DataFlow::Node pred, DataFlow::Node succ) {
110	  exists(DataFlow::CallNode call |
111	    (
112	      call.getTarget().hasQualifiedName("io", "ReadAll") or
113	      call.getTarget().hasQualifiedName("io/ioutil", "ReadAll")
114	    ) and
115	    pred = call.getArgument(0) and
116	    // ReadAll returns (bytes, error). Track taint into result 0, the bytes, only.
117	    // The error result is an I/O or decode failure string, never response data,
118	    // so tracking it would flag code that merely prints that error.
119	    succ = call.getResult(0)
120	  )
121	  or
122	  exists(DataFlow::CallNode call |
123	    call.getTarget().hasQualifiedName("bufio", "NewScanner") and
124	    pred = call.getArgument(0) and
125	    succ = call
126	  )
127	  or
128	  exists(DataFlow::MethodCallNode read |
129	    (
130	      read.getTarget().hasQualifiedName("bufio", "Scanner", "Text") or
131	      read.getTarget().hasQualifiedName("bufio", "Scanner", "Bytes")
132	    ) and
133	    pred = read.getReceiver() and
134	    succ = read
135	  )
136	}
137	
138	// The asciisanitizer wrap is the blessed barrier. Both Sanitizer{} and
139	// &Sanitizer{} forms are accepted, regardless of which fields are set.
140	predicate isSanitizerBarrier(DataFlow::Node n) {
141	  exists(DataFlow::CallNode c, Type argTy |
142	    c.getTarget().hasQualifiedName("golang.org/x/text/transform", "NewReader") and
143	    argTy = c.getArgument(1).getType() and
144	    (
145	      argTy.hasQualifiedName("github.com/cli/go-gh/v2/pkg/asciisanitizer", "Sanitizer") or
146	      argTy
147	          .(PointerType)
148	          .getBaseType()
149	          .hasQualifiedName("github.com/cli/go-gh/v2/pkg/asciisanitizer", "Sanitizer")
150	    ) and
151	    n = c
152	  )
153	}
154	
155	// Structured decoding is trusted. Both `json.Unmarshal` and
156	// `(*json.Decoder).Decode` go through cli/cli's REST clients, which are built on
157	// go-gh's sanitizing transport: for JSON content types the body is sanitized
158	// before any decode. A decoded value is therefore not raw external content.
159	predicate isStructuredDecodeBarrier(DataFlow::Node n) {
160	  exists(DataFlow::CallNode c |
161	    c.getTarget().hasQualifiedName("encoding/json", "Unmarshal") and
162	    n = c.getArgument(0)
163	  )
164	  or
165	  exists(DataFlow::MethodCallNode c |
166	    c.getTarget().hasQualifiedName("encoding/json", "Decoder", "Decode") and
167	    n = c.getReceiver()
168	  )
169	}
170	
171	// iostreams.Untrusted.String() returns content with ANSI escapes neutralized, so
172	// its result is sanitized. Raw and RawBytes are the deliberate opt-out and are
173	// intentionally NOT barriers, so a value taken out through them stays tracked to
174	// the terminal (unless the destination is ContentOut, which sanitizes itself).
175	predicate isUntrustedStringBarrier(DataFlow::Node n) {
176	  exists(DataFlow::MethodCallNode c |
177	    c.getTarget().hasQualifiedName("github.com/cli/cli/v2/pkg/iostreams", "Untrusted", "String") and
178	    n = c
179	  )
180	}
181	
182	module UnsanitizedResponseConfig implements DataFlow::ConfigSig {
183	  predicate isSource(DataFlow::Node n) {
184	    isResponseBodyReader(n) or isBase64DecodeSource(n)
185	  }
186	
187	  predicate isSink(DataFlow::Node n) {
188	    exists(DataFlow::CallNode call, int i |
189	      (
190	        call.getTarget().hasQualifiedName("fmt", "Fprint") or
191	        call.getTarget().hasQualifiedName("fmt", "Fprintln") or
192	        call.getTarget().hasQualifiedName("fmt", "Fprintf")
193	      ) and
194	      isTerminalBoundWriter(call.getArgument(0)) and
195	      not isContentOutWriter(call.getArgument(0)) and
196	      i >= 1 and
197	      n = call.getArgument(i)
198	    )
199	    or
200	    exists(DataFlow::CallNode call |
201	      (
202	        call.getTarget().hasQualifiedName("io", "Copy") or
203	        call.getTarget().hasQualifiedName("io", "CopyBuffer")
204	      ) and
205	      isTerminalBoundWriter(call.getArgument(0)) and
206	      not isContentOutWriter(call.getArgument(0)) and
207	      n = call.getArgument(1)
208	    )
209	    or
210	    exists(DataFlow::MethodCallNode call |
211	      call.getTarget().getName() = "Write" and
212	      isTerminalBoundWriter(call.getReceiver()) and
213	      not isContentOutWriter(call.getReceiver()) and
214	      n = call.getArgument(0)
215	    )
216	  }
217	
218	  predicate isBarrier(DataFlow::Node n) {
219	    isSanitizerBarrier(n) or isStructuredDecodeBarrier(n) or isUntrustedStringBarrier(n)
220	  }
221	
222	  predicate isAdditionalFlowStep(DataFlow::Node pred, DataFlow::Node succ) {
223	    isReaderConsumptionStep(pred, succ)
224	  }
225	}
226	
227	module UnsanitizedResponseFlow = TaintTracking::Global<UnsanitizedResponseConfig>;
228	
229	import UnsanitizedResponseFlow::PathGraph
230	
231	from UnsanitizedResponseFlow::PathNode source, UnsanitizedResponseFlow::PathNode sink
232	where
233	  UnsanitizedResponseFlow::flowPath(source, sink) and
234	  not sink.getNode().getFile().getRelativePath().regexpMatch(".*_test\\.go") and
235	  not sink.getNode().getFile().getRelativePath().regexpMatch("internal/fake_vuln/.*") and
236	  not sink.getNode().getFile().getRelativePath().regexpMatch("\\.github/codeql/tests/.*")
237	select sink.getNode(), source, sink,
238	  "HTTP response content reaches a terminal writer that is not IOStreams.ContentOut. " +
239	  "Write external content to opts.IO.ContentOut, or wrap it with the asciisanitizer."
240
